response.markdown_report:
The best first experiment remains a **learned recency residual added to SASRec**, evaluated through controlled perturbations. At 0% research progress, its small implementation cost favors it over a new architecture; usefulness remains unproven because SASRec already learns historical relevance [5].

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training margins measure fitted separation, not generalization. Training pseudo-holdouts remain contaminated by fitting. (2) Twenty users suggest that broad associations dilute recent, specific matches; they cannot establish population effects. (3) The compatibility interface supports architecture changes, provided diagnosis uses the actual module and restores its prior training mode.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Shuffle studies motivate controls for catalog evolution and last-item effects [1,2]. Sensitivity alone cannot demonstrate intent understanding. (2) Multi-window modeling motivates temporal separation without validating this residual [3]. (3) Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog rankings [4]; pinned validation remains the selection criterion.

Three directions follow: measure temporal reliance; test a minimal recent-history pathway; and assess text-supported relevance with abstention when evidence is absent.

| Framework component | Existing approach | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | SASRec sequence features | Recent embedding residual | Recent activity may reflect satisfied demand |
| Diagnosis | Training margins and geometry | Paired history perturbations | Reliance does not establish intent |
| Evidence | Titles/descriptions | Explicit text matches | Compatibility and user need remain uncertain |
| Selection | Pinned validation HR@10 | Same metric and routing | Full-catalog behavior may differ |

Three atomic ideas remain candidates. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paired recent-versus-old deletion audit [1,2] | 4/7/5 | Controlled, reusable diagnostic | No direct ranking improvement; masking needs care |
| Learned recency residual [3,5] | 3/6/4 | Cheap, testable recency hypothesis | Familiar mechanism; may amplify redundant demand |
| TF–IDF title/description residual | 3/5/4 | Uses permitted evidence | Surface overlap can reproduce reported errors |

**Selected algorithm.** At every causal prefix, exponentially average nonpadding item embeddings, normalize, and add a bounded residual to SASRec features.

```python
rho = exp(-1 / 5)  # fixed interaction-step horizon
u = rho * u + mask * sqrt(d) * embedding
z = rho * z + mask
fused = mask * (sasrec_feature + sigmoid(alpha) * layer_norm(u / z.clamp_min(eps)))
score = dot(fused, unscaled_candidate_embedding)
loss = existing_training_loss(score, positives, negatives)
```

Initialize the gain near 0.05; update every prefix, diagnostic hook, checkpoint, and predictor writer consistently. Preserve baseline splits, seeds, loss, optimizer, and epochs.

Predeclare eight controls: exactly disabled residual, trainable logit scale, uniform pooling, last-item pooling, fixed-gain recency, learned-gain recency, detached residual embeddings, and timestamp decay. Fix checkpoint rules and stop within 43,200 GPU-seconds, including failures and diagnostics; do not expand the grid.

Use frozen-model paired perturbations with unchanged targets/candidates: matched recent/older deletions, position-preserving masking versus compaction, and repeated last-item-preserving shuffles. Keep readout fixed and verify attention masking. Report target-rank changes, HR@10 changes, overlap, missing-evidence counts, and within-category user-bootstrap intervals. Training-only targets measure fitted reliance; genuine predictive generalization requires events excluded from fitting [6]. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Fixed candidates and bootstrap intervals do not remove validation-selection optimism or establish intent, compatibility, or simulator traits.

idea.description: Add one learned, bounded recency residual coefficient to each dataset’s SASRec representation. Combine ordinary SASRec features with a normalized exponentially weighted mean of item embeddings from each observed causal prefix, then score candidates through the existing target embedding table.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback identifies insufficient emphasis on specific recent interests. A small residual tests this hypothesis while retaining the baseline sequence representation. SASRec already learns historical relevance, so recency behavior alone does not establish a missing capability. Controlled pooling, scale, and gradient comparisons are necessary before attributing improvement to recency.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], baseline loss/optimizer/batching, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Keep execution single-GPU and artifacts beneath each trial directory. No new datasets or pretrained weights are needed.

For each prefix, use x_t = sqrt(d) * item_emb(sequence_t), validity mask m_t, fixed rho = exp(-1/5), u_t = rho*u_(t-1) + m_t*x_t, and z_t = rho*z_(t-1) + m_t. Set r_t = u_t/clamp(z_t, eps), apply parameter-free F.layer_norm(r_t, (d,), weight=None, bias=None), and explicitly zero padded fused outputs. Set gamma = sigmoid(alpha), initializing alpha = log(0.05/0.95). Keep decay fixed in the selected experiment; learning decay is a later hypothesis outside this search. Multiply fused features by unscaled candidate embeddings, matching baseline target scaling. The recurrence costs O(BLd) work, O(Bd) running state, and O(BLd) retained prefix/autograd memory; a Python loop adds L sequential launches while SASRec attention cost remains unchanged.

Make log2feats(sequence) return fused B x L x d features everywhere. Define predict_score explicitly: aligned item IDs B x L produce B x L scores; aligned candidate IDs B x L x K produce B x L x K scores; final features B x d with shared candidates K or per-user candidates B x K produce B x K scores. Use explicit shape checks and operations rather than ambiguous broadcasting. For nonempty left-padded inference inputs, use the final fused feature at index -1. Save the gain, decay horizon, architecture identifier, and baseline configuration; update the predictor writer to reconstruct and load the identical trained architecture.

Predeclare eight configurations, each covering all four datasets: (1) the exact baseline with a residual bypass, (2) baseline with positive trainable global logit scale initialized to 1, (3) uniform-history residual with fixed gain 0.05, (4) last-item residual with fixed gain 0.05, (5) fixed-gain geometric residual with gain 0.05, (6) selected learned-gain geometric residual, (7) configuration 6 with both history-side and candidate-side residual embeddings detached while keeping the backbone gradients and gain trainable, and (8) configuration 6 with timestamp decay. Normalize pooling outputs identically. For configuration 8, use prefix-available elapsed times and a fixed dataset horizon of five times the median strictly positive adjacent training-history gap, calculated from training interactions only. If timestamps cannot support this definition, mark this configuration unavailable without adding a substitute. Timestamp recurrence uses elapsed time between valid events and leaves padding state unchanged.

Match shared-parameter initialization, minibatches, negative samples, optimizer, and training duration across configurations. Fix checkpoint evaluation at every completed epoch, select by the host-compatible four-category macro validation HR@10, and resolve checkpoint ties by earliest epoch and configuration ties by the listed order. Plan runs using measured runtime and stop before exceeding the shared 43,200 GPU-second cap, including diagnostics, debugging, and failed trials. Report unfinished configurations explicitly; do not expand the grid. A gate-disabled inference pass on a residual-trained checkpoint measures branch dependence, but cannot replace training the exact baseline bypass. Inference-only positive scaling cannot change ranks; training-time scaling can change optimization.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model as the trained module; save its prior training flag, call eval(), use no_grad(), and restore the flag in a finally block. Return metrics and metric_definitions, including sample counts, thresholds, perturbation settings, and null values for unavailable measurements. Preserve existing embedding geometry and margin statistics, explicitly stating that these measure fitted behavior. Category metadata is unavailable, so retain empty category lists with an availability flag rather than inferred categories. Never use unavailable ratings, review text, prices, stores, or unobserved diversity/conformity traits.

For additional diagnostics, take each eligible training user's final training event as a fixed diagnostic target and restrict input to preceding events. Label this as fitted-model reliance because the target participated in fitting. Use diagnostic seed 42 to draw 99 unique negatives from the dataset catalog, excluding the target and the user's original training history; freeze candidates, exclusions, and deterministic tie-breaking across every intervention. These candidate sets are separate from pinned host validation candidates. Do not resplit the benchmark or claim that removing the target from probe input removes training influence. Any generalization claim must rely on targets excluded from fitting; the pinned validation remains the available selection evidence and is subject to repeated-selection optimism. Global temporal leakage cannot be repaired by a diagnostic intervention without changing the benchmark split [6].

Use the same eligible users with at least six prefix events. Delete k = min(3, floor(prefix_length/2)) most recent events, explicitly including the final event, versus k oldest events and k uniformly sampled events. Report position-preserving evidence removal separately from compaction. For position-preserving removal, retain original positions and the original prediction-query slot while removing deleted item evidence from attention keys/values; do not substitute an untrained mask token. Verify that the actual encoder permits the required query and attention masks; otherwise report this intervention unavailable. Compaction repacks surviving events using the normal left-padding path and therefore changes adjacency and positional distances. For shuffling, permute only earlier valid events, retaining the last item, item multiset, length, and padding. Use five seeded permutations and aggregate repetitions within each user.

Report paired target-rank changes, diagnostic HR@10 changes, top-10 overlap, eligibility counts, and results by dataset, history length, and target training-popularity bin. Bootstrap users within each category with 2,000 seed-42 replicates, preserving paired conditions and equal-weight category macro-averaging. Aggregate perturbation repetitions before resampling. These 95% percentile intervals quantify uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; they do not capture training-seed variability, remove target contamination, establish causal preferences, or correct validation-selection optimism. Keep twenty-user full-catalog feedback as qualitative evidence rather than population evaluation. Report title/description availability and abstain from compatibility or need claims without explicit evidence; potential repeated-title redundancy is not proof of unwanted ownership.

Verify recurrence outputs and gradients against explicit causal geometric sums; verify padding invariance, causal independence, and consistent training/diagnostic/inference logits in evaluation mode. Confirm checkpoint round-trip parity and exact disabled-control baseline scores and gradients. These checks establish implementation consistency, not benchmark improvement. No performance gain is claimed before execution.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare the eight configurations and the shared search-budget cap.
For each affordable complete configuration:
  For each of the four datasets:
    initialize the shared SASRec parameters with training seed 42
    initialize alpha = log(0.05 / 0.95) when the gain is learned
    for each baseline training batch:
      H = baseline_SASRec_features(sequence)
      u, z = zeros(B, d), zeros(B, 1)
      for t in causal sequence order:
        m = sequence[:, t] != 0
        x = sqrt(d) * item_emb(sequence[:, t])
        u = rho * u + m[:, None] * x
        z = rho * z + m[:, None]
        r = parameter_free_layer_norm(u / clamp_min(z, eps))
        F[:, t] = m[:, None] * (H[:, t] + sigmoid(alpha) * r)
      positive_scores = dot_aligned(F, unscaled_item_emb(positive))
      negative_scores = dot_aligned(F, unscaled_item_emb(negative))
      optimize the unchanged baseline loss on valid target positions
    evaluate checkpoints under the pinned validation protocol
    save model, architecture settings, decay, gain, and matching predictor writer
Select only by equal-weight four-category validation HR@10, with declared tie-breaking.
Freeze selected models and run fixed-candidate paired perturbation diagnostics.
Report fitted reliance separately from validation selection and full-catalog qualitative feedback.
Stop before the shared GPU-second cap; do not add configurations.

originality.positive: The combination of a minimal residual with explicit pooling, scale, gradient, and perturbation controls produces a clear task-specific hypothesis.
originality.negative: Recency pooling, bounded residual gains, and shared-embedding scoring are established mechanisms; the proposal adds limited architectural novelty.

future_potential.positive: The controlled comparisons can reveal whether recent-item aggregation contributes beyond SASRec and can guide later temporal or content-based extensions.
future_potential.negative: Recent interactions cannot distinguish continuing demand from a need already satisfied, and gains on sampled validation candidates may not transfer to full-catalog recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: The selected model adds one scalar per dataset and a causal pooling recurrence without extra encoders, external data, or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable attention-mask interventions, detached-gradient controls, consistent predictor serialization, and budgeted paired evaluation require more work than the residual alone.

related_work.title: [1] Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes original-versus-shuffled history comparisons across 15 datasets, motivating tests of whether order contributes predictive value.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity does not identify user intent or establish the benefit of the proposed residual.
Last-item-preserving shuffles probe earlier ordering conditional on the final interaction; small effects do not establish that all temporal information is unnecessary.

related_work.title: [2] Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes random shuffling from shuffling constrained by item availability, highlighting catalog evolution as a possible explanation of sequential signal.
limitations: Availability controls require reliable availability information; first observed interaction timestamps are only proxies.
The proposed perturbations do not independently resolve catalog-evolution confounding.

related_work.title: [3] MIMAR-SRec (2026)
contributions: The supplied summary describes intent modeling across temporal windows with robustness to interaction, temporal, and preference noise.
limitations: It motivates temporal separation but does not validate this simpler residual on the matched RecHarness task.

related_work.title: [4] Sampled recommendation metric analysis (IJCAI 2021)
contributions: Identifies systematic problems with sampled recommendation metrics, supporting separation of sampled-candidate selection and full-catalog diagnostics.
limitations: Does not remove the requirement to use the task's pinned evaluation protocol or predict which proposed model will improve it.
Fixed candidates improve comparability but do not establish full-catalog ranking quality.

related_work.title: [5] Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (SASRec)
contributions: Introduces self-attentive sequential recommendation with causal historical representations.
Provides the backbone against which additional recency aggregation must demonstrate incremental value.
limitations: Attention and historical relevance modeling do not themselves establish observed user intent.
The original model does not provide evidence that this proposed residual improves the matched benchmark.

related_work.title: [6] Time to Split
contributions: The supplied summary documents how splitting choices change sequential-model rankings, motivating explicit separation of fitted reliance and predictive generalization.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned benchmark splits.
Deleting a fitted target from diagnostic input cannot erase its training influence.

related_work.title: [7] Inference at Scale
contributions: The supplied summary supports bootstrap and randomization-based inference for comparative evaluation.
Motivates paired user-level uncertainty estimates with perturbation repetitions aggregated within user.
limitations: Bootstrap intervals cannot correct contaminated targets, repeated validation selection, or unmeasured training-seed variability.

related_work.title: [8] SASRec original implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for causal prefix features and item-embedding scoring.
limitations: The actual RecHarness baseline remains authoritative for parameter scaling, masking, loss, and predictor compatibility.

related_work.title: [9] PyTorch LayerNorm documentation
contributions: Documents layer normalization and the distinction between normalization and learned affine parameters.
limitations: Normalization ensures implementation consistency but does not establish equal optimization effects or recommendation gains.
